ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The main body in the figure is a transition-state/reaction structure: on the left there is a cyclohexene ring, with a C=C double bond drawn inside the ring; the upper-right position of the ring is connected to a carbonyl carbon, the carbonyl oxygen is above, and a C=O double bond is drawn; the right side of the carbonyl carbon is connected to a carbon chain, in which there is a C=C double bond and which continues to connect to the terminal carbon. Above the figure there are also H⁺ and a curved arrow, but the problem asks to ignore the arrow, and H⁺ is not counted as a non-hydrogen bond. Reasoning count: Count the bonds between non-hydrogen atoms by region, and count a double bond as one bond. The cyclohexene ring has a total of 6 intraring C-C bonds, among which the intraring double bond is still counted as 1 bond. The connecting bond from the ring to the carbonyl carbon is 1. The carbonyl C=O double bond is counted as 1. The single bond from the carbonyl carbon to the right-side carbon chain is 1. The C=C double bond in the right-side carbon chain is counted as 1. The C-C single bond from after this double bond to the terminal carbon is 1. The total is 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11.

raw_record.question_text: In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen. Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First describe the image components, then count non-H bonds region by region. Count the six C-C bonds around the cyclohexene ring, including the ring double bond as one bond. Add the bond from the ring to the carbonyl carbon. Add the C=O double bond as one bond. Add the single bond from the carbonyl carbon to the right-hand carbon chain, the C=C double bond in that chain as one bond, and the final C-C single bond to the terminal carbon. Sum: 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11.

method.method_draft: Construct the non-hydrogen connectivity graph from the drawing. The six-membered ring contributes 6 graph edges. The substituent attached to the ring contributes one edge from ring carbon to carbonyl carbon, one edge from carbonyl carbon to oxygen, one edge from carbonyl carbon to the side-chain carbon, one edge for the alkene connection in the side chain, and one edge from that alkene carbon to the terminal carbon. The total number of heavy-atom edges is 6 + 5 = 11.
